scope: Thirteenth expansion batch: 12 exercises, three characteristic-pattern mono da items, three recurring-past recollections, three casual mono/mon reasons, and three explanatory wake da conclusions. This does not cover every normative, emotional or lexical use of mono.

sources.section: Mono da for characteristic or expected patterns, conventions and common-sense judgments. This supports the descriptive use, not a claim that every mono da sentence is an unqualified universal rule or a prescription.

Past-form mono da for looking back on how things used to be, often nostalgically or introspectively. The claim that all inconsequential past events instead require ta koto ga aru is not adopted; occurrence, habitual recollection and other past statements are different choices.

Sentence-final mono/mon as emotionally colored reasons, including explanatory nda/nanda before them. Casual/childlike or insistent effects are relevant, but the source's blanket advice to avoid mon in all standard conversation is not adopted.
Wake da as a reasoned explanatory conclusion or no-wonder understanding. The source's universal equivalence with English so is not adopted.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original and require independent linguistic review. A source-backed pattern does not automatically attest an invented sentence.

The first six questions visibly request the supplied verb's dictionary or ta form before printed mono desu. The same three verbs occur on both sides. Their current-characteristic versus recurring-past framing is explicit; ta-form alone is not claimed to prove nostalgia in every mono da sentence.
A past recollection need not be pleasant or prove that the old behavior or state has ceased. The umbrella example is reflective, while the gathering and snow examples are nostalgic.

The other six questions visibly request exactly the endings mono, mon or wake da as written. Mono and mon share one answer class. Other spellings, kara, extended nda mono/mon endings or other inference expressions are outside this controlled task, not globally ungrammatical.
The first-time item already prints nanda. Its n is from explanatory no, while the added mon is from mono. The exact missing span must not duplicate the printed material.

Screen the full article inventory. Generic mono da can overlap with normative statements in some contexts; wake can provide explanations in other communicative settings. The tasks specify the function rather than infer it from an unstated nuance.
All prior 170 exercise records remain unchanged against preservationBaseline. One SRS identity per exercise, not per verb spelling, mono/mon realization or choose/type presentation.
